newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Menatep sees ADR price about $2 per share.
newsitem.headline: Russia Menatep sees ADR price about $2 per share.

text.p: Bank Menatep, Russia's 11th biggest bank by assets, plans to get no less than $2 per share in its first level-one American Depositary Receipts issue, a bank spokesman said on Tuesday.
"The $2 is our shares' current price on the local market and we shall kick off from here," Pavel Yerasov told Reuters.
He said the bank planned to launch ADRs at the start of 1997.
Previously the bank said it planned to issue ADRs by the end of 1996. The delay was due to the fact that the project was not a priority for the bank, Yerasov said.
The bank has not yet decided whether it will be a private or a public offering.
One ADR covers 10 shares with a dual face value of $1 and 1,000 roubles.
Another big Russian bank, Inkombank, plans to get $0.8 per share through ADRs, where one ADR equals 15 shares with a face value of 1,000 roubles.
Yerasov said the Bank of New York, Menatep's depositary, was carrying out an advertising campaign abroad to promote the bank's ADRs.
He said the bank was in talks with potential investors, but declined to name them.
He also said Menatep, like Inkombank, did not plan to find a lead manager for the project. ING-Eurasia is Menatep's custodian.
Menatep can sell no more than three percent of its 100 billion roubles authorised capital through the placement.
Banking shares are very illiquid in Russia and only one, for Bank Sankt Peterburg, is traded on the Russian Trading System.
